meta.title: Cannae
meta.eyebrow: 2 August 216 BC · Apulia · Second Punic War
meta.subtitle: Hannibal yields the centre, turns the flanks and closes the most famous double envelopment in ancient warfare.

sun.note: August sun and wind are approximations; ancient local time and calendar conversion are uncertain.

meta.strengthNote: Polybius gives about 80,000 Roman infantry and just over 6,000 cavalry against a Carthaginian force of just over 40,000 infantry and 10,000 cavalry [poly]. The Roman headline includes 10,000 men left in camp; they are shown separately and captured after the field battle. Losses across moments are illustrative allocations of Polybius's totals, not a casualty return. Livy's lower Roman death total (48,200) is shown in the debate notes [livy].
meta.method: This is a tactical reconstruction, not a surveyed battlefield map. Unit positions are placed on a modern terrain window around Canne della Battaglia using Polybius's relative order (Romans facing south; Carthaginians north; Carthaginian cavalry left/right and African flank reserves), checked against two schematic maps [poly] [wp] [roth]. The ancient Aufidus channel and exact battle location are unsettled; all coordinate-level claims are low confidence [mahaney]. Modern terrain is shown only as a relief context.
meta.notes: The two Roman camps and Hannibal's camp are shown schematically. No historical map overlay is offered because the available maps are tactical diagrams rather than georeferenceable surveys. Heights are exaggerated; woodland, roads and the exact river trace are illustrative. The intentionally coarse unit groupings are a readability choice, not evidence for exact tactical subdivisions.

phases.label: Deployment
phases.title: A battle on uncertain ground
phases.text: Varro brings the troops from both Roman camps across the Aufidus and faces south. Polybius gives about 80,000 Roman infantry and more than 6,000 cavalry. Hannibal's line faces north: Spanish and Celtic cavalry by the river, Africans on the flanks, the Spanish-Celtic centre forward, and Numidians on the far wing [poly].
tactic: A centre gives ground without breaking while strong wings turn inward. It only works if the enemy keeps pressing into the pocket.
events: Cannae and the ancient river course anchor the reconstruction, but not an exact battlefield grid [mahaney]
phases.debate: The ancient Aufidus channel and exact field are disputed. These coordinate placements are illustrative; Polybius's relative deployment is the higher-confidence claim [poly] [mahaney].

phases.label: Skirmishers
phases.title: The front screens collide
phases.text: The advanced guards begin the fight. Polybius says neither side gained an advantage in this preliminary contest; the main infantry and cavalry are still forming their decisive relationships [poly].
tactic: Light troops can occupy and test an enemy while the main formation remains intact.
events: Skirmishers engage before the heavy infantry [poly]

phases.label: Cavalry decision
phases.title: Hasdrubal breaks the Roman right
phases.text: The Spanish and Celtic horse defeats the Roman cavalry near the river. At the same time the heavy infantry begins its struggle; the Roman mass pushes into the projecting Spanish and Celtic centre [poly].
tactic: Close-order cavalry can decide a wing quickly, then exploit its mobility elsewhere.
events: The Roman right-wing cavalry gives way [poly]

phases.label: The centre yields
phases.title: The Roman mass presses into the crescent
phases.text: The Spanish and Celts fall back under the pressure of the legions. Polybius's key point is sequential contact: the centre was engaged before the African wings, so the pursuing Roman mass advanced into the gap [poly].
tactic: A formation can conceal its intended shape until the enemy's commitment makes a response too late.
events: The centre's controlled withdrawal draws the Roman mass forward [poly]

phases.label: Flanks close
phases.title: The Roman mass is pinched from both sides
phases.text: First the Africans turn inward against both exposed Roman flanks. Hasdrubal has crossed to the other cavalry wing, but the rear is still open: this moment is the pinch, not yet the completed ring [poly].
tactic: A force attacks front and flank together, denying the enemy room to face every threat.
events: Western African wing turns into the Roman flank [poly]
Eastern African wing turns into the other flank [poly]
Hasdrubal wins the second cavalry fight and can ride behind the Roman mass [poly]

phases.label: Cavalry seals the rear
phases.title: The ring closes behind the Romans
phases.text: Only now does Hasdrubal's cavalry arrive behind the Roman mass. The Africans keep both flanks pinned while cavalry closes the northern exit and the rallied Spanish and Celtic centre holds the front, while the Numidians pursue the broken allied horse. Polybius describes Romans turning in small groups to meet attacks from every direction [poly].
tactic: A force that has won a wing can turn mobility into a rear attack before the enemy can re-form.
events: Hasdrubal's cavalry seals the Roman rear [poly]
The trapped Roman mass has no room to turn or deploy [poly]
Paullus is killed in the infantry struggle [poly]
phases.debate: The sequence of the final slaughter is much clearer than its duration. This model uses hourly moments only to make the tactical relationship legible, not to assert an exact stopwatch chronology [poly] [livy].

phases.label: Destruction and flight
phases.title: The Roman army collapses
phases.text: Polybius reports about 70,000 Roman dead, 10,000 captives not in the main battle, and only about 3,000 infantry escaping the field; he gives 5,700 Carthaginian dead. Livy gives a much lower Roman death total. The strength chart follows Polybius while preserving this disagreement [poly] [livy].
tactic: Pursuit turns a defeated army into a destroyed one, but the sources must distinguish field losses, camp captures and fugitives.
events: Polybius's loss total is adopted for the chart; Livy's lower figure remains a live disagreement [poly] [livy]
phases.debate: Polybius: about 70,000 Roman dead and 5,700 Carthaginian losses. Livy: 48,200 Romans killed and 8,000 Carthaginians killed. Ancient casualty figures cannot be reconciled here; both are reported, and neither makes the coordinate reconstruction more certain [poly] [livy].

units.name: Roman citizen cavalry
units.note: Roman cavalry on the right beside the river in Polybius's order; it was defeated by Hasdrubal's Spanish and Celtic horse [poly].

units.name: Roman legions
units.note: The Roman citizen heavy infantry, packed more deeply and closely than normal [poly].

units.name: Italian allied infantry
units.note: Allied heavy infantry forms the other half of the unusually deep Roman mass [poly].

units.name: Roman light troops
units.note: Light infantry was posted in front of the line, opened the battle with the opposing skirmishers, then fell back through the maniples [poly].

units.name: Italian allied cavalry
units.note: Allied cavalry on the Roman left was held by the Numidians until Hasdrubal arrived [poly].

units.name: Roman camp garrison
units.note: Polybius says Lucius left 10,000 infantry in the camp; Hannibal's camp guard trapped and captured them after the field victory [poly].

units.name: Spanish and Celtic centre
units.note: Spaniards and Celts formed the projecting centre. Polybius says it yielded under pressure, drawing the Roman mass between the Africans [poly].

units.name: African heavy infantry, western wing
units.note: African heavy infantry held back on the flank, then faced inward against the Roman side [poly].

units.name: African heavy infantry, eastern wing
units.note: The second African wing mirrors the inward turn described by Polybius [poly].

units.name: Slingers and javelin troops
units.note: Hannibal sent slingers and javelin troops forward before the main line crossed and deployed [poly].

units.name: Spanish and Celtic cavalry (Hasdrubal)
units.note: Hasdrubal's cavalry defeated the Roman right, then rode across to decide the other cavalry fight and attack the infantry's rear [poly].

units.name: Numidian cavalry (Hanno)
units.note: Numidians kept the allied cavalry occupied; Hasdrubal then joined them and left them to pursue the fugitives [poly].

hq.name: Varro
hq.note: Command alternated by day; Polybius makes Varro commander on the battle morning [poly].

hq.name: Paullus
hq.note: Paullus rode from the Roman right into the infantry fight and was killed there [poly].

hq.name: Hannibal and Mago
hq.note: Hannibal and Mago commanded the centre [poly].
